name: Mpiemo
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.note: Wikipedia: 'little description of the language'; only Festen 2008 subclassification named on Glottolog

sources.citation: Festen, Bradley D. 2008. Verbal tone in Mpyemo. MA thesis, University of North Dakota, Grand Forks (advisor Steve Parker). UND Scholarly Commons, Theses and Dissertations 4474, ix+108 pp.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request); access check: online with a university library login
sources.note: Nothing: 0 hits for stress/accent/prominence in the 118-page text layer. It analyses Mpyemo as a two-tone (H/L) language with three surface pitch levels via a tone-raising rule ('There are three phonetic pitch levels in Mpyemo, but I will argue for only two underlying tone heights: high and low', p. 7); TBU assumed to be the syllable (p. 8); §1.7 segmental overview (pp. 19ff.) covers 20 consonants, 7 vowels, contrastive vowel length; boundary tones are 'grammatical morphemes, rather than intonational in nature' (p. 8). Record found via UND OAI-PMH (oai:commons.und.edu:theses-5477); the common…

sources.citation: Thornell, Christina & Yasuko Nagano-Madsen. 2004. Preliminaries to the phonetic structure of the Bantu language Mpiemo. Africa & Asia: Göteborg working papers on Asian and African languages and literatures 4: 163-180.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request); access check: online with a university library login
sources.note: Nothing about stress. Acoustic study (vowels, long vowels, implosives, labialised velars, prenasalised stops) of the Nola (CAR) variety, one main informant; tone marked impressionistically as high/low (p. 166 fn. 4); notes long vowels 'tended to have a lower pitch' (p. 168) and that 'a phonetically long vowel could have a different tone within it' (p. 169); F0 of word-initial nasal compared with prefix /a/ (p. 176). No word on accent/stress. downloaded from GUPEA (handle 2077/84756) via the DSpace REST API.

sources.citation: Hammarström, Harald, Christina Thornell, Malin Petzell & Torbjörn Westerlund. 2008. Bootstrapping language description: the case of Mpiemo (Bantu A, Central African Republic). Proceedings of LREC 2008, Marrakech, pp. 3350-3354.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Only a one-line typological note (§3, p. 3350): 'The language has SVO basic constituent order and has tones, but the tonal distinctions appear to have a low functional load.' Also states 'The[re] is no published grammatical description of Mpiemo'. Nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Thornell, Christina. 2005. Minoritetsspråket mpiemos sociolingvistiska kontext (Special survey article 2/2005). Africa & Asia 5: 167-191.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Sociolinguistic survey in Swedish; useful bibliography of the SIL manuscripts (Beavon 1978/1986/n.d., Fester 2002). Nothing on stress or tone.

sources.citation: Thornell, Christina. 2004. Wild plant names in the Mpiemo language. Africa & Asia 4: 57-89.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Ethnobotanical name list; remarks that an orthography fitting 'the phonetics and phonology of the Mpiemo language still needs to be devised'. Nothing on stress or tone.

sources.citation: Thornell, Christina. 2003. Data on the verb phrase in the Mpiemo language. Africa & Asia 3: 91-122.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Questionnaire sentence data (Cloarec-Heiss verb-phrase questionnaire, Nola 2000); transcription 'in part phonological', tone not marked except a footnote that 3rd person positive vs negative 'a' differ 'by length or tone' (p. 116 fn. 1). Nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Cheucle, Marion. 2014. Étude comparative des langues makaa-njem (bantu A80): phonologie, morphologie, lexique. Vers une reconstruction du proto-A80. Thèse de doctorat, Université Lumière Lyon 2 (NNT 2014LYO20071).

sources.note: Comparative phonology of eight A80 languages including Mpiemo, in French; the per-language phonology synthesis is the most likely place for an explicit remark on accent/stress vs tone in Mpiemo, and it summarises the unpublished SIL/Bangui sources.
